title: Citation-coverage lint tool (machine-enforced provenance-on-every-assertion)
context: PLAN.md v0.2 adds a machine-enforced citation-coverage lint as an M0 exit criterion: every assertion sentence in a datasheet must carry a citation anchor, and the lint feeds the documentation-completeness score. The 90/100 bar is not reviewer-judged on this dimension -- the lint enforces it mechanically. The lint runs in CI and fails if any assertion lacks a provenance citation. This is distinct from provenance-008 (which is a snapshot-capture tool for license text and release metadata). Binding cancer guardrails apply: open-access / aggregate / de-identified data only; no medical advice. Code is MIT-licensed and must pass pnpm build && pnpm test && pnpm lint.
objective: Build a citation-coverage lint tool that parses a datasheet, detects any assertion sentence lacking a citation anchor, fails CI on uncited assertions, and outputs a per-section coverage score feeding the documentation-completeness metric.
acceptanceCriteria: Lint parses a datasheet document and detects any assertion sentence lacking a citation anchor (per the citation-anchor convention defined in the canonical metadata model).
Fails CI with a named list of uncited assertions (file, section, line) when citation coverage is not 100%.
Outputs a per-section citation-coverage score that feeds the documentation-completeness metric; does not replace reviewer judgment on other completeness dimensions.
Committed golden fixtures include a failing datasheet (at least one uncited assertion) and a passing datasheet (all assertions cited), exercised in CI; no real inspected data committed.
Code MIT-licensed; pnpm build && pnpm test && pnpm lint green; DCO signed-off; no credentials or secrets committed.
